messages.text: For a AI use case involving AI data centers, where would Vector Network Analyzer fit in the test workflow?

A Vector Network Analyzer would fit in the **signal-integrity / high-speed interconnect validation part of the AI data-center test workflow**, especially around **PCB/PCBA transmission channels, connectors, cables, and possibly optical-interconnect related VNA setups**.[20][21]
### Workflow placement and role
| Workflow point | Where VNA fits | Role |
|---|---|---|
| AI data-center interconnect context | AI/data-center connectivity includes high-speed electrical interconnect, optical interconnect, fiber, power, cooling, and related infrastructure.[9] High-speed electrical connectivity includes paths from ASIC packages to system endpoints and products optimized for signal integrity, multi-lane pluggable architecture, and up to 224G/lane PAM4 cable assemblies.[14] | The VNA is relevant to the high-speed electrical channel portion, not the whole data-center facility workflow.[9][14] |
| Transmission-channel validation | The high-speed digital validation flow identifies the transmission channel as Tx package, PCBs, connectors, and Rx package, and separately lists signal-integrity flow items such as insertion loss, crosstalk, eye diagram, and TDR impedance.[36][37] | The VNA belongs where the channel is characterized for SI behavior, especially loss and impedance-related measurements.[36][37] |
| PCB fabricator / system-house PCB test flow | R&S PCB test solutions place testing across Material Measurement, Material/Stackup selection, Signal Integrity modeling/testing, Sampling testing, and PL/Process Monitoring, with items including impedance/TDR, DK/DF extraction, IL, roughness, Xtalk, TL modeling, eye diagram, and Delta-L.[4][5][50] | In this flow, the VNA would be used around SI modeling/testing and sampling/process checks for IL and impedance/TDR-related channel verification, while material/stackup data feed the channel model.[4][5] |
| AI server / data-center supply-chain mapping | In the AI server ecosystem mapping, R&S ZNA/ZNB are listed for server PCB IL and TDR, connector/cable high-speed cable testing, PCBA high-speed trace test, switch VNA usage, and optical VNA setups for silicon photonics.[20][21] | This directly maps VNA usage to AI-server-related PCB, cable/connector, switch, and silicon-photonics test entry points.[20][21] |
| Practical probing / de-embedding workflow | Case material shows VNA-based PCB/interconnect probing setups using VNA, probes, mount-kit, de-embedding tools, and local partner support; cited DUTs include board-to-board connectors, bare-board PCB probing, socket/interconnection tests, and measurements such as impedance, insertion loss, and return loss.[24][25] | The VNA is not just a bench instrument; it is part of a channel-measurement setup with probes/fixtures/de-embedding to remove fixture effects and characterize the DUT channel.[24][25] |
【推論】For an AI data-center use case, place the VNA **after material/stackup planning and during channel SI validation**, then reuse it in **sampling or process monitoring** for PCB, cable, connector, and high-speed trace checks, because the cited workflows list those stages and the AI-server mapping assigns ZNA/ZNB to IL, TDR, high-speed trace, and high-speed cable tests.[4][20][21]
R&S product examples supported by the passages are **R&S ZNA**, a Vector Network Analyzer family covering ZNA26/ZNA43/ZNA50/ZNA67 up to 67 GHz, with time-domain analysis/TDR option ZNA-K2 and extended time-domain analysis including eye diagram option ZNA-K20, and **R&S ZNB3000**, a Vector Network Analyzer family with base frequency range up to 43.5 GHz and frequency-upgrade option up to 54.0 GHz.[29][31][35][62]

A Vector Network Analyzer would fit in the **signal-integrity / high-speed interconnect validation part of the AI data-center test workflow**, especially around **PCB/PCBA transmission channels, connectors, cables, and possibly optical-interconnect related VNA setups**.[20][21]
### Workflow placement and role
| Workflow point | Where VNA fits | Role |
|---|---|---|
| AI data-center interconnect context | AI/data-center connectivity includes high-speed electrical interconnect, optical interconnect, fiber, power, cooling, and related infrastructure.[9] High-speed electrical connectivity includes paths from ASIC packages to system endpoints and products optimized for signal integrity, multi-lane pluggable architecture, and up to 224G/lane PAM4 cable assemblies.[14] | The VNA is relevant to the high-speed electrical channel portion, not the whole data-center facility workflow.[9][14] |
| Transmission-channel validation | The high-speed digital validation flow identifies the transmission channel as Tx package, PCBs, connectors, and Rx package, and separately lists signal-integrity flow items such as insertion loss, crosstalk, eye diagram, and TDR impedance.[36][37] | The VNA belongs where the channel is characterized for SI behavior, especially loss and impedance-related measurements.[36][37] |
| PCB fabricator / system-house PCB test flow | R&S PCB test solutions place testing across Material Measurement, Material/Stackup selection, Signal Integrity modeling/testing, Sampling testing, and PL/Process Monitoring, with items including impedance/TDR, DK/DF extraction, IL, roughness, Xtalk, TL modeling, eye diagram, and Delta-L.[4][5][50] | In this flow, the VNA would be used around SI modeling/testing and sampling/process checks for IL and impedance/TDR-related channel verification, while material/stackup data feed the channel model.[4][5] |
| AI server / data-center supply-chain mapping | In the AI server ecosystem mapping, R&S ZNA/ZNB are listed for server PCB IL and TDR, connector/cable high-speed cable testing, PCBA high-speed trace test, switch VNA usage, and optical VNA setups for silicon photonics.[20][21] | This directly maps VNA usage to AI-server-related PCB, cable/connector, switch, and silicon-photonics test entry points.[20][21] |
| Practical probing / de-embedding workflow | Case material shows VNA-based PCB/interconnect probing setups using VNA, probes, mount-kit, de-embedding tools, and local partner support; cited DUTs include board-to-board connectors, bare-board PCB probing, socket/interconnection tests, and measurements such as impedance, insertion loss, and return loss.[24][25] | The VNA is not just a bench instrument; it is part of a channel-measurement setup with probes/fixtures/de-embedding to remove fixture effects and characterize the DUT channel.[24][25] |
【推論】For an AI data-center use case, place the VNA **after material/stackup planning and during channel SI validation**, then reuse it in **sampling or process monitoring** for PCB, cable, connector, and high-speed trace checks, because the cited workflows list those stages and the AI-server mapping assigns ZNA/ZNB to IL, TDR, high-speed trace, and high-speed cable tests.[4][20][21]
R&S product examples supported by the passages are **R&S ZNA**, a Vector Network Analyzer family covering ZNA26/ZNA43/ZNA50/ZNA67 up to 67 GHz, with time-domain analysis/TDR option ZNA-K2 and extended time-domain analysis including eye diagram option ZNA-K20, and **R&S ZNB3000**, a Vector Network Analyzer family with base frequency range up to 43.5 GHz and frequency-upgrade option up to 54.0 GHz.[29][31][35][62]
